segments.text: SANAA: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis on Saturday said they targeted a range of Saudi assets in the past 24 hours, listing three airports including capital Riyadh’s, two oil facilities, a pipeline and an air base.

newsDocuments.headline: UAE’s Ras Al Khaimah shuts all beaches as neighbours grapple with oil leak

segments.text: DUBAI: Ras Al Khaimah authorities said on Saturday that all beaches in the emirate would be closed until further notice, a day after an offshore oil leak prompted beach closures in neighbouring Umm Al Quwain and Sharjah.

The United Arab Emirates said on Friday that efforts were underway to contain oil leaking from a tanker offshore, with its Ministry of Climate Change and Environment conducting an environmental assessment.
UAE authorities have not named the tanker involved in the incident or said what caused the spill.

newsDocuments.headline: Raw sugar steadies as oil rallies, weather concerns persist

segments.text: LONDON: Raw sugar futures on ICE steadied on Friday as oil prices rallied and El Nino-linked weather concerns persisted, while coffee gained.

Consumers and traders are likely to have come in on the buy side, seeing good value after the recent falls as there is no shortage of bullish drivers in the market, said consultant Michael McDougall. These include excess El Nino-linked rain
Sugar was benefiting from surging energy prices, which encourage mills to ramp up production of the cane-based biofuel ethanol, at the expense of sugar.
